title: Terzaghi Filter Retention Criterion
applicability: Original criterion. Modern practice uses NEF criteria (more conservative for fine-grained bases).

title: Seepage Through Homogeneous Dam (Dupuit Approximation)

q.description: Seepage per unit length of dam

applicability: Very approximate. Assumes horizontal flow (Dupuit). Flow net or numerical analysis required for design.

title: Exit Gradient FS Against Piping
applicability: FS ≥ 3–5 for dam foundations. i_exit from flow net or seepage analysis.

title: Blanket Theory — Seepage Exit Gradient (Infinite Blanket)
applicability: USACE blanket theory for underseepage analysis. Simplified closed-form for uniform blanket.

title: Wave Runup (SMB Method Simplified)
equation: R = 0.5 × H_s (for smooth slopes); R = 0.75 × H_s (for rough riprap)

R.description: Wave runup height above still water level

applicability: Simplified. Full calculation uses SMB or CEM methods with fetch, wind speed, and slope angle.
source: USACE Shore Protection Manual, USBR DS-13 Ch. 6

title: Freeboard Requirement
equation: Freeboard = Wave runup + Wind setup + Settlement allowance + Safety margin
applicability: Minimum freeboard: typically 1.5–3 m above maximum water surface for large dams. Must be above PMF level.

title: Riprap Sizing (USBR Simplified)
equation: D₅₀ = H_s / 2.2 (for 2H:1V slope); D₅₀ = H_s / 1.4 (for 3H:1V slope)
applicability: Angular riprap, properly placed. Minimum layer thickness = 1.5 × D₅₀.

title: Kenney & Lau Internal Stability Criterion
equation: H/F ≥ 1.0 for all grain sizes between D₂₀ and D₉₀
applicability: If H/F < 1.0 at any point → potentially internally unstable → susceptible to suffusion.

title: Drain Capacity Check
equation: Q_drain = k_drain × i × A_drain ≥ Q_seepage × FS
applicability: Drains must have large excess capacity. Gradient through drain typically low (< 0.3).
